findings: The parser reports syntax errors in exactly the 4 chart components (AreaChart, BarChart, ComboChart, LineChart) at an ordinary arrow function with a typed parameter followed by a ternary on the next line: const calculateHeight = (height: number | undefined) =>\n  height ? Number(height) + 15 : 60. That valid TSX is misparsed, and the arrow 'calculateHeight' is lost in all 4 files (4 missed definitions). Everything else in the 4 files was still extracted, and the status text says definitions inside unreadable regions may be missing.

Lists of a component's users omit JSX uses written through a renamed import: import { Calendar as CalendarPrimitive } and <CalendarPrimitive .../> at DatePicker.tsx:639 and :941 leave an extracted reference unresolved and no edge, so find_callers for Calendar misses the date picker.

The one low-tier tsx edge is wrong: <Icon .../> inside Callout, where Icon is a prop, is bound to an unrelated Storybook export named Icon in tooltip.stories.tsx. A prop component bound to a same-named story export is the same class of error as in the other languages.
SingleProps extends Omit<PickerProps, 'translations'> gets no EXTENDS edge: a repository supertype wrapped in a generic utility type is not recorded.

The first-8 recall rule produced 40 of 40 right, but the sample is easy (cx(...) and local helper calls dominate). JSX uses of repository components in the same five files: 39 of 41 bound (the 2 unbound are the renamed import), plus 4 <CustomTooltip> uses of a prop alias with no repository target.

Precision was clean in the sampled high tier (30 of 30), but 19 of the 30 sampled edges have a story file as caller; there is no medium tier and a single low edge, so the tiers say little about harder cases.
Calls and component usage share one edge kind: a JSX use <TimeSegment/> is stored as CALLS from the rendering component to the rendered one, which is the right direction.
